svg.text: Field IO and how the modules share it
Each module drives only its own IO; the coordinator (Fieldbus controller, else Wi-Fi + BLE, else LoRa) merges all IO into one image shared over the stack bus
(IO-6). Wi-Fi + BLE adds 6 DI, 4 DO, 4 AI and 2 relays; LoRa adds 4 DI, 4 DO and 4 AI.
Draft C.11 · 2026-11-22 · PRD 0.5 · prices at 100 units

g.text: Field IO on the Fieldbus-controller module — 28 channels
SPDT (NO + NC + COM), 10 A at 230 VAC
Total: 6 analog in + 10 digital in + 8 relays + 4 high-side out = 28 field IO
• DI3 changes → its module timestamps it → the coordinator updates the IO image → reports it at the next poll
• 4G module reads the change over the stack bus → publishes MQTT over TLS to the cloud
• Cloud asks for relay RL2 = ON through the 4G module → module sends a write request on the bus
• Coordinator checks: is the requesting module authenticated (keys in the MCU's TrustZone secure world) and the
configured owner of RL2? → drives RL2 → confirms back
• If the 4G module stops refreshing its ownership lease, RL2 returns to its safe state
• A remote LoRa node reports a tank level → the LoRa module in the stack forwards it to the coordinator
• The coordinator stores it as virtual point V-AI1 in the same image → visible to the cloud like a local input
• The Fieldbus controller's RS-485 port acts as Modbus RTU slave: AI / DI / DO mapped to registers
• Same owner rules apply: SCADA writes reach an output only if the RS-485 interface is its configured owner
outputs off if this MCU hangs

• Local hardware: each module reads and drives only its own IO (Fieldbus controller 28 channels; Wi-Fi + BLE 16 plus
RS-485 and CAN; LoRa 12 plus RS-485).
• Publish: the coordinator broadcasts the IO process image on the RS-485 stack bus cyclically (rate configurable, for
example 100 ms) and immediately on change, in its next transmit turn (≤ ≈ 20 ms).
• Read: any fitted module may read any input, status or virtual point.
• Write: each output has exactly one owner at a time — coordinator logic or one named module — set by configuration.
Writes from any other module are rejected and logged.
• Trust: only modules authenticated by the coordinator may write (SEC-5); strongest with the Fieldbus controller's
TrustZone (PSA L3). A cloned or rogue module can at most read.
• Lease and safe state: the owner refreshes a lease; if it lapses or the bus fails, the output goes to its configured
safe state. Independently, the hardware watchdog switches all relays and outputs off if its own MCU hangs (IO-4).
• Standalone: a module running alone uses its own IO and interfaces; no other module is needed.
